surveyTemplate.name: Azure WAF Transformation Pulse
surveyTemplate.description: Lightweight recurring pulse covering all 5 Azure Well-Architected pillars. Complements full WAF Assessments (04-import.md/03-manual-entry.md) with a quick quarterly check-in for transformation tracking (07-survey.md).

questions.prompt: Do you have explicit, documented availability/recovery targets (SLO/RTO/RPO) for your critical flows?
Are redundant components/instances in place for your most critical business flows?
Do you regularly run resiliency/chaos tests (failure and load injection) rather than relying on real incidents to find weaknesses?
Is there a tested, documented disaster recovery plan covering the whole system?
Is there a defined security baseline aligned to compliance/industry norms, with measurement against it?
Is identity/access management enforced with least-privilege and auditable controls across users and components?
Is data encrypted at rest and in transit using modern, platform-native methods aligned to data classification?
Are incident response procedures defined, owned, and rehearsed?
Is there a maintained cost model (initial/run-rate/ongoing) with a budget buffer?
Is daily cost data captured with trend/forecast visibility and automated anomaly alerts?
Are spending guardrails (policy/limits/gates) in place to prevent overspend?
Are unneeded or underused components/features regularly identified and right-sized or removed?
Is there a shared, blameless DevOps culture with continuous-improvement practices across teams?
Is infrastructure provisioned via Infrastructure as Code (preferring declarative approaches)?
Does your telemetry/observability design validate decisions and support continuous improvement?
Are releases deployed via small, gated, progressive rollouts with rollback plans?
Are numeric, requirement-driven performance targets set per critical flow?
Are Azure services/tiers chosen based on their ability to hit performance targets and absorb capacity changes?
Is performance testing regularly run in production-like environments against defined targets?
Is there clear ownership/communication for responding to live performance incidents?

_notes.perPillarBreakdown: 4 questions per pillar (RE/SE/CO/OE/PE) for balanced coverage, within the 10-30 recommended range in 07-survey.md
_notes.responseModel: Each SurveyResponse uses SurveyResponseLevel (VeryLow..VeryHigh, NotApplicable) per 02-data-model.md; optional numeric Score override.
_notes.domainCode/controlCode: Resolved to DomainId/ControlId at seed time by joining against the azure-waf.json fixture (Framework must be seeded first).
